data.body:
Review remediation record (2026-08-21) for this ticket's plan — moved out of the description to fit the plan-review admission cap. Five blocking findings were raised and corrected:

- Count contradiction. The Context section named THREE synthetic-timeout `_git` shims (`src/rebar/_store/push.py:71`, `src/rebar/_store/sync.py:66`, `src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py:64`) while AC3 said "the four". Three is correct; AC3 was corrected to say three.

- A verification that cannot pass. AC3 originally verified the shim deletion with `grep -rn "timed out after" src/rebar/_store`. That grep still matches `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:604` after a CORRECT implementation, because that occurrence lives inside the new shared `run_git`. It was replaced with an owner-exempt definition-count guard, per guard rule #4 in the parent epic `airborne-wellloved-kingfisher`.

- Signature contradiction. An earlier revision said `classify(result) -> GitOutcome` in Approach while the remediation section said the registry was keyed `(marker, operation)`. Those contradicted each other. Resolved in favour of `classify(result, *, operation) -> GitOutcome` taking the full result (`args`, `returncode`, `stdout`, `stderr`), because `_advisory_lock._is_cas_mismatch` discriminates on command shape and exit code, which no `(marker, operation) -> kind` table can express.

- The `cannot lock ref` over-merge. The earlier plan mapped every marker to exactly ONE `GitOutcome` kind. That is wrong for `cannot lock ref`, which carries three deliberately different, bug-hardened verdicts: retriable local lock (`gitutil._is_git_lock_error`); a push reject that is explicitly NOT a lease mismatch (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock_push.py:68` — bug 4afc established that only `stale info` is the `--force-with-lease` signal, since `cannot lock ref` also covers hook declines, rate limits, server errors and remote ref.lock contention; bug ebee added `fatal error in commit_refs` to the same non-CAS set); and advisory-lock-HELD, terminal (`_advisory_lock.py:305`, with exit 128 or exit 1). Collapsing them would re-open 4afc and ebee, so the registry is keyed by operation and the divergence is preserved.

- The missing tenth kind. The nine-kind enumeration had no home for the fifth classification site the plan itself names: `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:465` `_INVALID_OBJECT_MARKERS = ("invalid object", "error building trees")`, consumed by `_is_invalid_object_error`. That is git `write-tree` refusing a commit because an index entry references an object missing from the object DB, and its handler is a recovery (rebuild the index and retry), not a terminal failure. Folding it into FATAL would delete that recovery, so a tenth kind `INVALID_OBJECT` was added.
